description: A cash advance costs more than its upfront fee. In the example, $1,000 with a 5% fee, $3 ATM fee and 30 days of simple interest at 30% APR costs about $77.
definition: A credit-card cash advance may combine an upfront percentage/minimum fee, other fees and interest accruing from the transaction date.
explanation: A cash advance costs more than its upfront fee. In the example, $1,000 with a 5% fee, $3 ATM fee and 30 days of simple interest at 30% APR costs about $77.66 when fees are paid separately. Change the fee treatment and interest convention to match your agreement.
formula: Fee = max(amount × percentage, minimum) + ATM; interest follows the selected balance and daily-rate convention.

name: COBRA premium cost
title: COBRA premium cost: Worked Example and Limits
description: COBRA premium planning starts with the full plan cost, including the employer contribution. With $200 from the employee, $600 from the employer and a selec
definition: A COBRA premium estimate generally starts with the full applicable plan cost, including employer and employee contributions, rather than only the former payroll deduction.
explanation: COBRA premium planning starts with the full plan cost, including the employer contribution. With $200 from the employee, $600 from the employer and a selected 2% administrative charge, the monthly amount is $816 before any entered subsidy. This worksheet estimates premiums, not eligibility or total medical spending.
formula: Monthly payment = full plan premium × (1 + entered administrative rate) − entered subsidy.
formulaNote: Ordinary federal COBRA premium-only worksheet with a 0–2% administrative charge and constant entered monthly subsidy. Matching coverage tier, no eligibility or duration determination, medical spending, state continuation or disability-extension premium model.
